skill.name: using-agent-skills
skill.description: Discovers and invokes agent skills. Use when starting a session, or when you need to decide which skill or workflow applies to the piece of work at hand. This is the meta-skill that governs how all other skills are discovered and invoked.
skill.summary: Maps development tasks to the agent skill and workflow that best fits the work.
skill.author: addyosmani

content.value_statement: Teams often lose time choosing the right workflow for a software task. This skill maps task context to focused agent skills and a practical development sequence.
actual_capabilities: Classifies a task by development phase, such as planning, implementation, testing, or review.
Recommends a matching agent skill for common software engineering activities.
Shows when multiple skills should be applied in sequence.
Encourages explicit assumptions, active confusion management, and evidence-based verification.
Provides a quick reference of available skills and their intended purposes.
limitations: It does not implement code, run tests, or modify project files by itself.
Recommendations depend on the skills available in the surrounding repository.
It cannot resolve unclear requirements without information from the user.
The workflow sequence is guidance and may need adjustment for project-specific constraints.

use_cases.title: Route a New Feature
use_cases.description: Identify the right discovery, specification, planning, implementation, testing, and review skills before building a feature.

use_cases.title: Choose a Review Workflow
use_cases.description: Select focused review skills for quality, security, performance, or code simplification concerns.

use_cases.title: Orient a New Project
use_cases.description: Use the lifecycle sequence and quick reference to establish a consistent engineering process for an unfamiliar codebase.

prompt_templates.title: Find the Right Skill
prompt_templates.prompt: I need to [describe the task]. Which available agent skill should I use first, and why?

prompt_templates.title: Plan a Feature Workflow
prompt_templates.prompt: I am building [feature]. Recommend the skills I should apply in order, from requirements through verification.

prompt_templates.title: Resolve Competing Skills
prompt_templates.prompt: My task involves [concern A] and [concern B]. Identify the applicable skills, explain their order, and state any assumptions.

prompt_templates.title: Audit the Engineering Process
prompt_templates.prompt: Review this proposed workflow for [project task]. Identify missing skills, unclear assumptions, and verification gaps before implementation.

output_examples.input: I need to add an API endpoint and verify it.
output: Start with api-and-interface-design to define the contract.
Use incremental-implementation to build the endpoint.

output_examples.input: A production deployment needs a rollback plan.
output_examples.output: Use shipping-and-launch, with observability-and-instrumentation for monitoring and debugging-and-error-recovery for incident response.

best_practices: Describe the task and its current development phase before selecting a skill.
State assumptions and resolve confusion before starting non-trivial work.
Treat verification as part of every workflow, not as an optional final step.
anti_patterns: Do not apply a long skill sequence when a small task needs only focused guidance.
Do not continue when requirements or workflow responsibilities are unclear.
Do not skip testing, review, or runtime verification because the change looks simple.

faq.question: What does this skill do?
faq.answer: It helps select the agent skill or skill sequence that best matches a software engineering task.

faq.question: Does it write code?
faq.answer: No. It provides workflow guidance and routes the task to skills that can support implementation.

faq.question: Can multiple skills apply to one task?
faq.answer: Yes. Complex work may require skills for discovery, planning, implementation, testing, review, and release.

faq.question: Which tools support this skill?
faq.answer: The skill metadata lists Claude, Codex, and Claude Code as supported tools.

faq.question: What should I provide in my prompt?
faq.answer: Describe the goal, current phase, constraints, and any uncertainty that could affect the workflow.

faq.question: Does the suggested sequence always apply?
faq.answer: No. Use it as a starting point and adapt it to the task size, project rules, and verification needs.
